nodes.label: Gate 1 — the real-task input path
nodes.rationale: One real issue, end to end, on all four arms, with a precondition strong enough that a failure is attributable to the model. Implemented 2026-08-12 at schema 3.5.0; §6 is a three-pass review log of what the plan got wrong before any code was written.

nodes.label: Root cause A: no precondition on the harness INPUT
nodes.rationale: Every existing check is about the harness or a run's output; nothing asserts the thing handed to the agent is a task at all. That defect invalidated every Phase 0c capability figure. Six of six 'model failures' so far were harness defects -- the base rate is the argument for a gate that runs offline before any spend.

nodes.label: Root cause B: operational knowledge lived in a script
nodes.rationale: smoke_test.py was the only place that knew the proxy topology, credential paths, image build and config dump. A matrix driver beside it would either duplicate that knowledge -- so the gate and the real run drift into different environments and the gate stops gating -- or reach into a script from library code. Extraction into proxy.py and session.py is what keeps them one environment.

nodes.label: Task on disk: task.yaml plus reference.diff
nodes.rationale: One reference diff split at load, never two hand-maintained files. Two properties fall out and both are checked: the halves recompose to the original byte for byte, so nothing can be silently dropped; and a file that is neither half is a load error rather than a quiet omission.

nodes.label: Start state is base_sha plus the committed test half
nodes.rationale: A real bug-fix PR carries the test that proves the fix, and at base_sha that oracle does not exist -- so the self-correction loop has nothing to run against, the same truncation that invalidated Phase 0c arriving through the dataset instead of the image. Recorded as a methodology decision: handing over the oracle makes the task 'make this test pass', while a hidden oracle makes difficulty depend on the agent's test-writing habits. The setup commit uses a fixed author/date/message so start_sha is a pure function of the manifest and can be pinned.

nodes.label: Generated per-task Dockerfile
nodes.rationale: Generated rather than hand-written because the two most expensive ways a task image can be wrong are structural and a generator makes them impossible: USER root makes Claude Code refuse bypassPermissions, and an inherited ENTRYPOINT turns the container's sleep into an immediate exit. Both read as total model failure. `pip install -e .` is required -- a non-editable install resolves imports to site-packages so the agent's edits do nothing and every arm fails identically.

nodes.label: Preflight: the per-task discrimination precondition
nodes.rationale: Offline, no credentials, no spend, per task before the matrix starts: red before the reference fix and green after it, in this task's own image. The load-bearing detail is the exit code -- pytest's 1 means tests ran and failed while 2/3/4/5 mean the environment is broken, so `returncode != 0` would accept the exact Phase 0c failure as evidence the bug is present. Also checks non-root, claude version, git/rg, empty entrypoint, a clean tree after the suite, and no task-local CLAUDE.md.

nodes.label: Matrix driver: round-major ordering, resume, containment
nodes.rationale: Every (task, arm) appears once per round, shuffled under a recorded seed, so repeats are separated by a whole round -- the strongest separation available -- while staying reproducible. Resume is mandatory rather than nice, because run_id is deterministic and write_run opens mode 'x', so a second invocation against the same log raises. One cell's exception must not cost the other 2,399 and must not be swallowed either.

nodes.label: Resume guard on task_version and image digest
nodes.rationale: task_version is not part of run_id, so editing a task and re-running leaves every existing cell looking complete and silently mixes records of the old and new task under one task_id -- the most damaging hole in draft 1, and exactly the class Gate 1 exists to close. Version mismatch is a hard per-cell refusal; image-digest mismatch only warns behind --allow-mixed-images, because images legitimately rebuild and refusing would make resume useless.

nodes.label: What the matrix gates on vs. what the smoke test gates on
nodes.rationale: smoke_test's run_problems is the Phase 0c capability criterion, where no diff is a NO-GO. The matrix asks a different question -- a model failing a task is the data it is collecting -- so the driver checks only what makes a record uninterpretable (config dump, empty wire log, lost attribution, isolated=False) and never stops a run from being written.

nodes.label: task_set_commit and the 3.4.0 version bump
nodes.rationale: SCHEMA_VERSION moves even though no field is added: in 3.3.0 an empty task_set_commit means 'no dataset exists', in 3.4.0 it means 'this task declared none'. Same bytes, different claim -- the case the versioning rule exists for. A defect in the plan's own dirty-marker (a relative pathspec matching nothing) was caught by running it, not by reading it.

nodes.label: First real task: pallets/click #3360 / PR #3434
nodes.rationale: Chosen because its tests assert rendered behavior rather than an internal name, so a different-but-correct fix passes -- the rejected alternative (#3678) pins an arbitrary storage name and would score a correct alternative fix as a failure. Hermetic and fast (1,614 tests in 1.4s), and unlike the fixture it forces real navigation. It also surfaced that per-task dependency pinning is mandatory: the suite does not collect under the base image's pytest 9.1.1.
